definitions.explanation: Not famous or well-known. Used to describe people, places, or things that have not gained recognition or fame.
Having no name attached, or the identity is not known or disclosed.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{無名|むめい}の{画家|がか}だった。
{無名|むめい}の{新人|しんじん}がいきなり{優勝|ゆうしょう}した。
examples.english: An unknown newcomer suddenly won the championship.

examples.japanese: {無名|むめい}の{小|ちい}さな{村|むら}が、{映画|えいが}のロケ{地|ち}になったことで{一躍|いちやく}{有名|ゆうめい}になった。
examples.english: A small, obscure village suddenly became famous after being used as a filming location.

examples.japanese: {無名|むめい}の{詩|し}が{見|み}つかった。
{美術館|びじゅつかん}には{無名|むめい}の{作者|さくしゃ}による{中世|ちゅうせい}の{絵画|かいが}が{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: The museum displays medieval paintings by anonymous artists.

examples.japanese: この{刀|かたな}は{無名|むめい}だが、{刀身|とうしん}の{出来|でき}から{名工|めいこう}の{作|さく}と{推定|すいてい}されている。
examples.english: This sword is unsigned, but based on the quality of the blade, it is presumed to be the work of a master smith.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Used as a noun ({無名|むめい}) and as a no-adjective modifier ({無名|むめい}の).

SIMILAR WORDS:
{無名|むめい} (unknown/nameless) is the opposite of {有名|ゆうめい} (famous). The pair {無名|むめい}/{有名|ゆうめい} shares the same structure: {無|む}/{有|ゆう} (without/with) + {名|めい} (name/fame).

SPECIAL USAGE:
In the context of Japanese swords, {無名|むめい} (also read むめい) specifically means the blade lacks the swordsmith's inscription ({銘|めい}) on the tang.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無名|むめい}の{画家|がか}: unknown painter
- {無名|むめい}の{新人|しんじん}: unknown newcomer
- {無名|むめい}{戦士|せんし}: unknown soldier
- {無名|むめい}の{作者|さくしゃ}: anonymous author
